meta.face: A young man of about twenty-nine, pale from consumption, with a LONG, rather rectangular face — a high, broad forehead, a long straight nose with a rounded tip, light-brown eyes under HEAVY upper lids, raised to heaven, softly arched brows, lightly hollowed cheeks, a small mouth with a fuller lower lip, a rounded chin; thick, STRAIGHT dark-brown hair cut short and combed back from the brow, the ears showing; clean-shaven; the head tilted to his right. Not Aloysius's round face and curly hair.
meta.basis: No portrait was painted in his life; a wax mask of his face was taken after his death in 1755 (the shrine's 'Apoteosi'). The card follows the traditional portrait reproduced on Commons (unknown painter): a pale, long-faced young man with short straight brown hair, heavy-lidded eyes raised, in the black habit and white collar, holding a crucifix. The skull is his attribute (Wikipedia).
meta.excerpt: The notice he had hung on the door of his room in his last illness, «Qui si sta facendo la volontà di Dio, come vuole Dio e per tutto quel tempo che piace a Dio», as given in the Vita di San Gerardo Maiella on the shrine's site (ch. L'ultima malattia e la morte, §212); our rendering (he died in 1755)
